All 43 tests in `LexerAgentTest` (the only `*AgentTest.java` file in the project) pass.

I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `Lexer`:

- Lifecycle/state: `close()`/`isClosed()`, `getFirstEol()`, `getCharacterPosition()`, `getCurrentLineNumber()`, `getBytesRead()`.
- Predicate methods: `isEndOfFile`, `isStartOfLine`, `isQuoteChar`, `isEscape`, `isCommentStart`, `isDelimiter` (single-char, multi-char match/mismatch), `isEscapeDelimiter` (match and mismatch).
- `readEndOfLine` for LF, CR, CRLF, and non-EOL input.
- `readEscape` for named escapes (`r`,`n`,`t`,`b`,`f`), pass-through meta-characters, unexpected characters (returns `EOF`), and EOF during an escape (throws `CSVException`).
- `nextToken` end-to-end behavior: empty input, simple records, EOF with trailing data, quoted fields (plain, doubled quotes, unterminated with/without `lenientEof`, invalid trailing character, `trailingData` allowed), empty-line handling (ignored vs. not ignored, empty lines at EOF), comments (with/without trailing newline), surrounding-space trimming, and escaped delimiters/characters in simple tokens.
- `trimTrailingSpaces` boundary cases (trailing whitespace, all-whitespace, no whitespace).

Code is Java 8-compatible (no lambdas/diamond operators/underscored literals), matches the project's JUnit 5 style, and asserts on returned token types/content/flags rather than just absence of exceptions.
